proposed_comments.title: Determine More visibility from commands after the secondary action

confidence.rationale: The command model deliberately preserves separator entries, and content pages can retain the primary command ahead of the secondary command. Counting raw entries or assuming the first command is secondary therefore displays More when no command remains after the secondary action.

proposed_comments.body:
### Determine More visibility from commands after the secondary action

**Severity:** `medium`

`MoreCommands` retains separator entries and content pages can retain the primary command before the secondary command. Counting raw entries therefore leaves the More button visible when the secondary action is the last actionable item. Locate the actual secondary command and show More only when another command follows it.

```suggestion
    // MoreCommands can include separators and, for content pages, the primary command.
    // Only command items after the secondary command belong in the More menu.
    internal static bool ShouldShowMoreCommandsButtonFor(ICommandBarContext context) =>
        context.MoreCommands
               .SkipWhile(item => !ReferenceEquals(item, context.SecondaryCommand))
               .Skip(1)
               .Any(item => item is CommandContextItemViewModel);
```

proposed_comments.title: Preserve keyboard and context-menu behavior when More is hidden

confidence.rationale: The null-element open message is used by Ctrl+K and nested keybindings as well as the More button. After More is collapsed, opening must use a context-menu capability check and a visible anchor, and focus restoration must not target the collapsed button.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve keyboard and context-menu behavior when More is hidden

**Severity:** `high`

The null-element menu path is also used by Ctrl+K and nested keybindings, so it cannot be gated by More-button visibility. When More is hidden, opening the flyout must use the selected item's context-menu capability and anchor it to the visible secondary or primary command button. Focus restoration after closing the flyout also needs the same visible-button fallback; otherwise Escape can leave keyboard focus unset.

General note with no inline suggestion: these coordinated changes span the existing modified hunk and the focus-restoration method outside it, so they cannot be safely applied as an independent inline patch.
